title: BUEM GeoJSON Request Schema v4
description: Live request schema for the BUEM building energy model, promoted from draft 2026-08-14 -- see versions/v4/DRAFT.md for the full proposal/reconciliation/promotion history, and VERSIONING.md's v4.0.0 entry. Not formally reviewed by EnerPlanET line-by-line (see DRAFT.md's promotion note for what that does and doesn't mean). Each feature represents one building. The buem object contains four concerns: building (complete physical description — classification, geometry, and thermal performance), solver (execution settings), inputs (optional user-provided timeseries overrides), and weather (real-world weather-module data source selection). All measurable quantities carry an explicit unit field. SI units are assumed when unit is omitted. Dimensionless ratios use unit: '-'.

features.description: One entry per building to simulate

coordinates.description: [longitude, latitude, elevation?] — authoritative building location, used for weather station lookup

buem.description: BUEM model input. building contains the complete physical description of the building. solver contains execution settings. inputs contains optional user-provided timeseries that override model-generated values. weather selects which real-world weather-module data source feeds the thermal model -- a buem-side addition not present in EnerPlanET's own v4 as of the last check (2026-08-06), layered alongside their real inputs/solver.compute_cooling additions (see DRAFT.md for the reconciliation history).

building.description: Complete physical description of the building. Classification fields (type, country, etc.) sit at this level. Geometry and per-element thermal properties are in envelope. Building-wide thermal parameters are in thermal. When envelope is omitted, the model derives surface areas and U-values from the TABULA variant identified by building_type + construction_period + country. Reconciled against EnerPlanET's real v4 (2026-08-06): envelope is no longer required for this reason -- see https://github.com/enerplanet/buem-gateway/tree/main/schemas/v4.

name.description: Human-readable building label (e.g. '3434 · Single-family House'). Display only -- no effect on simulation. Reconciled from EnerPlanET's real v4 (2026-08-06).

A_ref.description: Reference floor area. Derived from floor element areas if omitted.

building_type.description: Buem-side proposal, live as of the v4 promotion (2026-08-14) -- enforced by geojson_validator.py against the union of RESIDENTIAL_BUILDING_TYPES and occupancy.SERVICE_BUILDING_TYPES (read live, not hand-copied). Still not present in EnerPlanET's real v4 as of the last check (2026-08-06, still free-text there, https://github.com/enerplanet/buem-gateway/tree/main/schemas/v4) -- see DRAFT.md's promotion note. TABULA residential size class (SFH single-family, MFH multi-family, AB apartment block, TH terraced house) or an occupancy service-building type id (supermarket, office, restaurant, school, hotel, bakery, warehouse, clinic). Determines whether internal-gains/electricity generation uses a household or service-building occupancy model.

capacity.description: Buem-side proposal, live as of the v4 promotion (2026-08-14). Not present in EnerPlanET's real v4 as of the last check (2026-08-06). Service-building capacity (seats/beds/staff) for occupancy generation. Ignored for residential building_type values, where household size applies instead. Omit to use the service type's own default capacity.

num_persons.description: Buem-side proposal, live as of the v4 promotion (2026-08-14, added 2026-08-07). Not present in EnerPlanET's real v4. Occupants per dwelling, passed to occupancy.HouseholdProfile. For a multi-dwelling building this is the size of one household, not the building's total occupancy -- see residential_units. Ignored for service-building building_type values, where capacity applies instead. Omit to use cfg_attribute.DEFAULT_NUM_PERSONS.

window_to_wall_ratio.description: Buem-side proposal, added to v4 2026-08-18 with explicit sign-off. Not present in EnerPlanET's real v4. Fraction of each exposed wall's area that is glazed, applied uniformly to every wall; each synthesized window inherits its host wall's own azimuth and tilt, so orientation follows the building's real geometry. Used only when 'envelope' supplies no window elements. Omit to use buem's own default.

residential_units.description: Buem-side proposal, added to v4 2026-08-18 with explicit sign-off. Not present in EnerPlanET's real v4. Number of dwellings in this building. Omit or send 1 for single-dwelling houses (SFH/TH); send the real dwelling count for apartment blocks and multi-family buildings (AB/MFH), where one feature represents the whole block. Scales the occupancy-generated internal gains and electricity load from one dwelling up to the whole building, matching the whole-block envelope the thermal solve uses.

archetype.description: Buem-side proposal, live as of the v4 promotion (2026-08-14, added 2026-08-07). Not present in EnerPlanET's real v4. occupancy household archetype (occupancy.households.archetypes.HOUSEHOLD_ARCHETYPES), selecting the occupancy-probability schedule shape. Residential only -- ignored for service-building building_type values. Omit to use cfg_attribute.DEFAULT_ARCHETYPE_BY_BUILDING_TYPE.get(building_type, 'generic') -- a first-pass heuristic, not a derivation; num_persons remains the dominant signal.

construction_period.description: TABULA construction-year class code for the building's country (e.g. "01", "02"), not a literal year range. Class boundaries are defined per country by each national TABULA dataset and are not consistent across countries. When envelope is omitted, this is looked up directly against the TABULA variant code (<country>.N.<building_type>.<construction_period>...) -- there is no year-range-to-class translation. Reconciled from EnerPlanET's real v4 (2026-08-06); buem's own example data still uses an older year-range convention pending a check of what buem's own TABULA lookup actually parses -- not changed here, see DRAFT.md.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g. NL, DE)

attic_condition.description: Attic conditioning status: - not applicable, N not conditioned, P partially conditioned, C conditioned, NI not insulated, PI partially insulated

cellar_condition.description: Cellar conditioning status — same codes as attic_condition

neighbour_status.description: Attached neighbours: B_Alone detached, B_N1 one shared wall, B_N2 two shared walls

equipment.description: Buem-side proposal, live as of the v4 promotion (2026-08-14; boolean-per-item shape as of the same date, replacing an earlier {mode,items} shape). Not present in EnerPlanET's real v4. Per-item household-equipment inclusion/exclusion: true forces the item to be treated as owned (bypassing occupancy's own ownership-probability draw for it), false forces it excluded entirely, and an omitted id falls back to occupancy's own default behavior for that item (including its normal stochastic ownership draw and any archetype-specific tuning). Keys are validated against the property list below -- additionalProperties: false rejects an unrecognized id at the schema layer, not just at runtime. Residential building_type only -- ignored (with a logged warning) for service-building types, since occupancy.ServiceBuildingProfile has no per-item equipment selection yet (see .claude/occupancy_module_activities.md). The property list is hand-copied from occupancy's households/data/equipment.json -- occupancy has no stable top-level export for this registry yet (same caveat building_type's enum carries for SERVICE_BUILDING_TYPES pre-promotion). Omit entirely to use occupancy's own default equipment set, unchanged.

envelope.description: All building surfaces. Each element carries both its geometry (area, orientation, tilt) and its thermal properties (U-value, solar gain coefficient, etc.) in a single entry. No separate thermal properties list is needed. Window/door/ventilation ('LOD3') elements are optional -- EnerPlanET's UI deliberately does not require filling them in. When elements of type window, door, or ventilation are omitted (or elements is supplied with wall/roof/floor only), the model synthesizes them internally from the supplied wall geometry, a matched TABULA archetype (building_type + construction_period + country), or documented safe-default ratios when no archetype matches (buem.buildings.mapping.live_synthesis; see buildings.rst 'LOD2 -> LOD3 in the live request-handling path'). An explicitly-supplied, non-empty set of window/door/ventilation elements is never overridden.

elements.description: List of all building surfaces. The id must be unique within the feature.

envelope_element.description: A single building surface. Geometry and thermal properties are defined together. For ventilation elements, no surface geometry is needed — only air_changes.

id.description: User-defined unique identifier for this surface element

name.description: Human-readable label for this surface (e.g. 'South Facade', 'Main Roof'). Display only -- no effect on simulation. Reconciled from EnerPlanET's real v4 (2026-08-06).

azimuth.description: Orientation measured clockwise from North (0=N, 90=E, 180=S, 270=W). For a window or door with parent_id set, this value is not independently authoritative: the model always forces it to match the referenced parent's own azimuth (a window/door cannot face a different direction than the wall/roof it's embedded in) -- a mismatch is corrected, not rejected. See parent_id.

tilt.description: Tilt from horizontal (0=horizontal roof, 90=vertical wall). Same parent_id-derived override as azimuth applies to windows/doors -- see parent_id.

parent_id.description: Id of the envelope element this surface is embedded in. Required for windows and doors. A window is embedded in a wall (or roof for a skylight); a door is embedded in a wall. When set, the child's own azimuth/tilt are ignored in favor of the referenced parent's azimuth/tilt (buem.buildings.mapping.live_synthesis.normalize_opening_azimuths()) -- this applies whether the child was supplied explicitly or synthesized internally (see the top-level building.envelope description for when synthesis happens). Not applied to ventilation elements, which carry no meaningful azimuth/tilt in this model (see thermal.n_air_use).

U.description: Thermal transmittance (U-value). Applies to wall, roof, floor, window, and door elements.

b_transmission.description: Transmission correction factor for elements adjacent to unheated spaces (e.g. cellar, attic). 1.0 = fully exposed to outdoor conditions. TABULA: b_Transmission_*

g_gl.description: Solar heat gain coefficient — window elements only. Fraction of incident solar radiation that enters the building. TABULA: g_gl_n_Window

air_changes.description: Air changes per hour — ventilation elements only

thermal.description: Building-wide thermal performance parameters aligned with IEE TABULA definitions. All fields are optional — model defaults (SI units) apply when omitted. Per-element thermal properties (U-value, g_gl, etc.) are defined directly on each envelope element.

n_air_infiltration.description: Uncontrolled air infiltration rate through gaps and cracks in the building fabric — TABULA: n_air_infiltration

n_air_use.description: Ventilation air change rate during building occupancy — TABULA: n_air_use

c_m.description: Internal thermal capacity per m² of floor area — how much heat the building structure can store. TABULA: c_m

thermal_class.description: ISO 13790 thermal mass class — used to derive c_m when c_m is not provided explicitly

comfortT_lb.description: Heating setpoint — minimum acceptable indoor temperature

comfortT_ub.description: Cooling setpoint — maximum acceptable indoor temperature

design_T_min.description: Outdoor design temperature used for peak heating load calculation — TABULA: Theta_e

F_sh_hor.description: Shading reduction factor for horizontal surfaces (e.g. roof) — TABULA: F_sh_hor

F_sh_vert.description: Shading reduction factor for vertical surfaces (e.g. walls, windows) — TABULA: F_sh_vert

F_f.description: Window frame area fraction — proportion of the window opening that is frame rather than glass. TABULA: F_f

F_w.description: Window non-perpendicularity correction factor — TABULA: F_w

phi_int.description: Internal heat gains from occupants, appliances, and lighting per unit floor area. Used in the ISO 13790 energy balance as a heat source that reduces heating demand and increases cooling demand. TABULA: phi_int. Typical residential: 3-5 W/m2. Default/description reconciled from EnerPlanET's real v4 (2026-08-06) -- previously had no default here.

q_w_nd.description: Net energy need for domestic hot water per unit floor area per year. Added to the heating energy need in the final energy balance. TABULA: q_w_nd. Typical residential: ~12.5 kWh/(m2.a). Unit fixed 2026-08-06: was "kWh/(m2a)" (no dot), which didn't match EnerPlanET's real v4 -- a real EnerPlanET request using their own documented unit string would have failed validation against this draft. Now matches theirs exactly.

F_red_htr.description: Intermittent heating reduction factor (ISO 13790 §13.2.2) — reduces effective transmission losses to account for night/weekend setback. TABULA F_red_htr1: 0.95 (AB/MFH) or 0.90 (SFH/TH).

weather_source.description: Buem-side proposal, live as of the v4 promotion (2026-08-14). Not present in EnerPlanET's real v4 as of the last check (2026-08-06, https://github.com/enerplanet/buem-gateway/tree/main/schemas/v4) -- their schema resolves weather from geometry.coordinates alone ("used for weather station lookup"), with no client-specified provider/year/percentile. Selects the real-world weather-module data source (T/GHI/DHI/DNI) for this building's location -- see UU-BUEM/weather. buem has no bundled/local-file weather fallback; every request is served by a real per-location fetch (unless profile is supplied). year and use_percentile/percentile are alternative ways to pick which year's data is used -- see each field's own description for how they interact. use_percentile/percentile remain schema-only -- not yet wired to real behavior, and explicitly rejected (not silently ignored) if sent -- see DRAFT.md's "Deliberately unwired at promotion".

provider.description: Which processed weather archive to fetch the location's T/GHI/DHI/DNI from. Each provider's processed archive only covers a specific calendar-year range (tightened 2026-08-14, per consultation -- a data-availability fact about each archive, not a buem design choice): era5-land 1980-2025, cosmo-rea6 1995-2018, merra-2 1950-2025. year (below) is validated against whichever provider applies (explicit or the merra-2 default) -- geojson_validator.py rejects an out-of-range combination at validation time, and the same ranges are expressed declaratively below via allOf/if/then for any other consumer validating directly against this schema file.

year.description: Calendar year to fetch weather for. The 1950-2025 bound here is the union across all three providers -- see provider's own description for each provider's real, narrower range, enforced by the allOf/if/then blocks below and by geojson_validator.py. Omit to use AttributeBuilder's own default year (currently 2018) -- does NOT fall back to the top-level start_time's calendar year (that was this field's original documented intent, but confirmed 2026-08-14 to risk silently requesting a year with no local archive; not implemented). Ignored if use_percentile is true -- percentile selects the year instead.

use_percentile.description: Buem-side proposal (2026-08-06). If true, select weather from a percentile climate year (see percentile) computed across the provider's full multi-year archive at this location, instead of the single specific year field. Schema-only -- not yet wired through buem's request-handling path, and explicitly rejected (not silently ignored) if sent; see DRAFT.md's "Deliberately unwired at promotion".

percentile.description: Buem-side proposal (2026-08-06). Which percentile climate year to use when use_percentile is true, ranked across the provider's available archive years for this location: P10 a cold/harsh-end year, P50 a typical/median year, P90 a mild/warm-end year. Ignored when use_percentile is false or omitted. Schema-only, same as use_percentile -- see its own description.

profile.description: Buem-side proposal, live as of the v4 promotion (2026-08-14). Not present in EnerPlanET's real v4. Caller-supplied hourly T/GHI/DHI/DNI weather timeseries, referenced by file path -- mirrors buem.inputs.electricity_load_profile's pattern. The file must be accessible inside the model container (shared Docker volume, BUEM_DATA_DIR). When provided, used directly instead of fetching from a weather-module archive; provider/year/use_percentile/percentile are ignored.

path.description: Absolute path to the profile file inside the container, with T/GHI/DHI/DNI columns (e.g. /data/profiles/5.3453464_52.4353446_weather_2018.json).

format.description: File format of the profile at path. json is EnerPlanET's actual format (confirmed 2026-08-14) and the default here accordingly -- a JSON array of hourly records, each {time, T, GHI, DHI, DNI} (time an ISO-8601 timestamp). csv/parquet remain supported for other/internal callers: first column the timestamp index, remaining columns T/GHI/DHI/DNI.

allOf.description: merra-2's processed archive covers 1950-2025 -- also the default provider, so this applies when provider is omitted too.

solver.description: Execution settings for the BUEM thermal solver. These control how the model runs and what it simulates.

use_milp.description: Use Mixed Integer Linear Programming solver (CVXPY + CBC) instead of the default scipy sparse solver. Slower but handles inequality constraints exactly.

compute_cooling.description: Reconciled from EnerPlanET's real v4 (2026-08-06). Enforce the upper comfort temperature bound in the LP solver. When false (default), the cooling constraint is omitted -- appropriate for buildings without active cooling, common in northern European residential buildings. When true, building.thermal.comfortT_ub is required and a cooling load profile is returned in the response.

parallel_thermal.description: Run heating and cooling simulations in parallel within a single building

use_chunked_processing.description: Process the 8760-hour timeseries in chunks to limit memory usage

inputs.description: Reconciled from EnerPlanET's real v4 (2026-08-06, https://github.com/enerplanet/buem-gateway/tree/main/schemas/v4). Optional user-provided timeseries inputs. When a field is present, it overrides the model-generated equivalent. When absent, the model generates the value from occupancy simulation.

electricity_load_profile.description: Hourly electricity consumption profile for the building, referenced by file path. The file must be accessible inside the model container -- use the shared Docker volume (BUEM_DATA_DIR) to make client files available. When provided, the profile is used directly as elecLoad (via occupancy.to_buem_profiles(elec_load=...), 2026-08-14) instead of the model-generated one -- Q_ig/occ_nothome/occ_sleeping still come from a real occupancy generation, only elecLoad itself is overridden. Electricity consumption heats the building interior and therefore affects heating and cooling demand. Supported formats: CSV (single column of values), JSON array, or gzipped JSON (.gz).

path.description: Absolute path to the profile file inside the container (e.g. /data/profiles/5.3453464_52.4353446_electricity_2018.csv)

unit.description: Unit of the values in the file. Defaults to kWh when omitted.

measurement.description: Base type for all measurable quantities. The unit field defaults to the SI unit for the quantity type when omitted.
